headline: Highest risk is data leakage: opik’s broad egress can transmit context while langchain4j provides no isolation or shared-channel controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between langchain4j and opik, and langchain4j has no io_surfaces or egress path shown that would let opik inject instructions into it by default. opik exposes REST API calls, but without a bridge this pairwise prompt-injection pathway is not evidenced.
conditions: IF an orchestrator copies opik output into langchain4j prompts automatically, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between them, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected except for explicit human-reviewed handoff.
Disable any automatic prompt templating from opik outputs.
Use separate workspaces with no shared drop folder.
Add content sanitization before any copy-paste bridge.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: opik has broad network egress and REST API calls, so if it receives sensitive context it can transmit it outward; langchain4j shows no egress and no data classes touched, so the main leakage risk is one-way from opik rather than symmetric. The pair lacks documented isolation, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF sensitive prompts or files are fed into opik, its broad egress can exfiltrate them.
IF both agents are placed in a shared workspace, accidental disclosure risk increases.
mitigations: Do not pass secrets or regulated data into opik.
Run opik behind an egress allowlist.
Separate workspaces and credentials for each agent.
Review REST destinations before enabling integrations.
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction on opik inputs and outputs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: langchain4j shows no write or network surfaces, while opik only advertises REST API calls and broad egress; there is no evidence that both can write the same mutable resource or share OAuth scopes. The pairwise write-conflict pathway is therefore limited and not documented.
conditions: IF both are wired to the same mutable REST resource, write conflicts become possible.
IF an external orchestrator grants shared credentials, contention risk rises.
mitigations: Use separate API credentials per agent.
Avoid pointing both agents at the same mutable backend.
Serialize writes through one coordinator.
Turn off unused REST integrations.
requires-engineering: add locking or optimistic concurrency controls.

D_cascading_error.rationale: opik’s REST-facing evaluation/observability role can consume outputs from langchain4j, and nothing in either profile shows a verification gate or critical review step. That makes an A-to-B handoff plausible in default integrations, so B may treat A’s output as authoritative unless the operator inserts checks.
conditions: IF langchain4j outputs are forwarded into opik without validation, errors can cascade.
IF opik is configured to act on evaluation results automatically, downstream mistakes amplify.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before opik consumes langchain4j output.
Require schema validation on all handoffs.
Log and diff A outputs before B processes them.
Disable automatic action-taking from evaluation results.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds and rejection rules.

E_compliance.rationale: Neither profile lists regulated data classes, residency constraints, certifications, or retention policies, so no compliance mismatch is evidenced. langchain4j and opik are both open-source with docs-only profiles, and the pairwise compliance pathway cannot be established from the available fields.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are later assigned to either agent, compliance review must be redone.
IF residency or retention settings are introduced, mismatch analysis changes.
mitigations: Document data classes before deployment.
Record residency and retention settings.
Review vendor/legal terms for any regulated workload.
Keep regulated data out of both agents until reviewed.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing by data class.
